This role reports to the Director of Sales and calls for an experienced strategic enterprise seller — someone with a substantial track record in high-level, strategic sales roles at manufacturing companies who embraces the value of planning, process, and execution against company and customer goals. This person is naturally driven to develop value-based relationships with customer executives, to build and execute co-developed strategic growth plans, and to work cross-functionally with both internal teams and customer stakeholders to deliver against those plans. Hadrian has strong access to stakeholders at Space and Defense primes, and a clear path to turn proof-of-concept manufacturing at the business-unit level into transformation programs at the corporate executive level. Success in this role depends on fluency in how Aerospace and Defense suppliers are qualified and onboarded. jobs.title: Growth Finance Manager
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Growth Finance owns the economics of how Hadrian wins work. We sit at the front end of every program — pricing the pursuit, shaping the deal, and structuring the partnerships and joint ventures that get new capacity off the ground with our commercial and government customers. The Associate is the analytical center of that work. You'll build the model behind a pursuit from a blank sheet: unit economics, capacity and capex requirements, rate and margin structure, and the returns case that determines whether we bid, at what price, and on what terms. You'll pressure-test your own assumptions before anyone else gets the chance, and you'll be expected to have a view — not just a spreadsheet — on whether a program is worth pursuing. Beyond the model, you'll help structure the vehicles. That means partnership and JV economics, term sheets, waterfall and downside mechanics, and the diligence behind counterparties we're considering taking risk with. You'll write the memo that goes to leadership, and you'll defend it in the room. This is a small team with a short path to owning deals outright. The work available to you scales with what you demonstrate rather than with tenure. You will work directly with the executive leadership team at Hadrian on some of the company’s most important strategic initiatives. jobs.title: Site Security Manager
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE Hadrian's Physical Security team protects the people, factories and export-controlled work behind Hadrian's growth. As we open new factories and bring on new teams, every site needs a security leader on the ground, and the program needs people who help build it across all of our sites. You will own security at our Torrance campus and be hands on every day: managing the contract security team, walking the site, and acting as the first call for any security risk. This is more than a walk-the-floor role. You'll also own a program area across every Hadrian site, such as investigations, workplace violence prevention, vendor management or security training, and help build a physical security program that keeps pace with the business. You'll partner with site leadership, Facilities, EH&S, People and the Facility Security Officer, and report to the Director of Physical Security. This is an on-site role in Torrance, CA. jobs.title: Security Systems & Technology Lead
jobs.description_text: The Role Hadrian's Physical Security team protects the people, factories and export-controlled work behind Hadrian's growth. We are opening new factories and facilities at a rapid pace, and every one of them needs security systems designed, built and commissioned to a single standard, so each new site is a standard package and not a new project. You will own the technology behind Hadrian's physical security program: access control, video surveillance and the systems around them, from security input on construction drawings through installation, commissioning and day-to-day administration. You'll set the standards, run several site builds and platform migrations at the same time, and hold integrators to the work. You'll partner closely with IT, Facilities, Information Security and the Facility Security Officer, and report to the Director of Physical Security. This is an individual contributor role based on site in Torrance, CA, San Francisco, CA or Mesa, AZ, with travel up to 30% to Hadrian sites. jobs.title: Build Engineer, Large Scale Machining
jobs.description_text: The Role Hadrian is looking for a Build Engineer, Large Scale Machining to own how our largest machined parts get made, including castings, forgings, plate weldments, and hull-scale structures. You will own each part from the first design review through qualification, ramp, and handoff to standard production. You are the bridge between the product and Capability Engineering: you interpret the product requirements, drive DFM, establish the build flow and sequence, and hand Capability Engineering a well-defined machining problem to solve. You will own new product and new process introduction for large machined parts end-to-end. Large parts are where precision gets hard: tight features are spread across multiple setups, and a datum scheme has to survive stress relief, flips, and weld. You set how each part flows through the factory, define the machining processes it needs, and work across Design, Supply Chain, Capability Engineering, Tooling, Quality, and Operations to bring it to rate. Decisions made during NPI set the cost, lead time, and quality of these parts for their life, and the processes you introduce become large-format machining capabilities Hadrian uses on the programs that follow. This role sits on the Build Engineering Commodities team alongside sheet metal and tube and pipe. It is hands-on. You will be at the machine for first parts, and you will own the outcome. jobs.title: Build Engineer, Castings
jobs.description_text: The Role Hadrian is looking for a Build Engineer, Castings to own large structural castings from the first design review through qualification, ramp, and handoff to standard production, whether we pour them, buy them, or run both paths in parallel. You are the bridge between the product and Capability Engineering: you interpret the product requirements, drive DFM, reverse engineer the product where the data is incomplete, establish the build flow and sequence, and hand Capability Engineering and the foundry a well-defined casting problem to solve. You will own new product and new process introduction for castings end-to-end. Many of the hardest products we build start as a casting, and decisions made at the pattern carry through machining, weld, and final assembly. You set how each casting is made and inspected, define the processes it needs, and work across Design, Supply Chain, supplier foundries, Capability Engineering, Quality, and Operations to bring it to rate. Decisions made during NPI set the cost, lead time, and quality of these castings for their life, and the processes you introduce become casting capabilities Hadrian uses on the programs that follow. They lead integration across every functional workstream, from diligence and pre-close planning through Day 1, Day 100, and the transition to business-as-usual. You'll report to the SVP, Public Policy, who sets the direction for the company's external affairs and holds the comms slate — the master calendar of everything Hadrian says publicly, sequenced across announcements, launches, executive moments, and policy pushes. Your job is to run Strategic Comms with full ownership of its craft and its team. You'll work in close partnership with peers across the broader external affairs function: a Brand & Marketing lead who owns owned channels, campaigns, and company events; and Government Relations and Policy leads who carry the company's positions into government offices and the broader policy ecosystem. jobs.description_text: Role Summary The Director, Forward Deployed Engineering leads the technical arm of Hadrian's Customer Programs motion. You sit inside Build Engineering and partner directly with the Customer Programs team, owning the manufacturing scoping of new customer engagements: translating what a customer wants into what Hadrian will actually commit to and build. This role works directly with customers every day. For many of them, you and your team are the face of Hadrian engineering, so how you show up in the room matters as much as the technical answer. The work starts with discovery. Before anything is proposed, you and your team get inside the customer's operation: observing how work actually flows, mapping their processes and constraints, and interviewing the people closest to the problem until you understand what they need, which is often different from what they first ask for. From there, you shape a solution that maximizes what the customer gets out of the engagement and builds toward where Hadrian is headed. The craft is steering to the answer where the customer's best outcome and Hadrian's direction reinforce each other: high impact, low effort, and built on what we already do well rather than new obligations we then have to invent our way out of. jobs.description_text: The Role You will take hard factory automation problems from ambiguity through production, and build the mechanical engineering team that does it with you. Few hardware teams are putting AI into the manufacturing or hardware design loop. We are, and we need leaders who are expert enough to push boundaries, yet humble enough to reinvent their own workflow. We are looking for leaders who want to build alongside their team, inventing new agentic workflows in a hybrid team of high performers to solve problems that were entirely out of reach even a year ago. jobs.title: CAD Modeler
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE: US defense systems run on technical data that is often decades old: scanned paper, hand-marked prints, partial models, and drawings that were never turned into 3D models. A part that exists only on an old drawing is hard to source. That slows how fast the armed forces and our prime customers can sustain and rebuild the systems that use it. Hadrian turns that data into manufacturing-ready models and drawings, so customers can keep their systems running and Hadrian can make or procure the parts. As a CAD Modeler, you build the 3D models and 2D drawings for naval and aerospace parts, starting from whatever the customer sends. You also build the models and drawings for each manufacturing state (M-state) of a part: the in-process configurations the factory builds and inventories on the way to the final part. Our engineers define each M-state, and you model, draw, and configure it. You own your parts from first model through release and every change after it. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Build manufacturing-ready 3D models from naval prints, aerospace drawings, partial models, and other customer documents, matching the customer's definition feature for feature. - Make the 2D drawings the factory runs on, from your models or the customer's. - Build the models and drawings for each M-state of a part. - Work out conflicting or unclear views against the rest of the drawing. - Keep PLM data correct and structured, and send your parts through the release workflow. - Carry each customer cha

jobs.title: IT Site Lead
jobs.description_text: The Role Hadrian is building a new precision manufacturing facility in partnership with Lockheed in Dallas/Fort Worth, Texas. We're looking for an Site Lead to own the buildout, day-to-day tech operations and serve as the face of Hadrian tech for the entire site. This is a hands-on role with real ownership: you'll manage endpoints, support manufacturing technicians and engineering staff, maintain local infrastructure, serve as the point person for day-2 vendors, and help visiting employees from other sites resolve issues while they're on-site. When fully operational you’ll support manufacturing technicians in the use of Hadrian’s proprietary AI platform Opus. You’ll act as a bridge between the customer and product providing valuable feedback directly from the factory floor to help further refine and develop the platform. As a remote extension of the central tech team, you'll also contribute to overall Helpdesk operations by supporting other Hadrian employees through Jira Service Management and co-managing the company's suite of SaaS tools. You'll report to the Manager of Tech Deployment and work closely with a central team covering IT, infrastructure, cybersecurity, network, and helpdesk across all Hadrian sites. jobs.title: People Programs Manager
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE: At Hadrian, we’re not just building autonomous factories — we’re building the teams, systems, and culture that will power the future of aerospace and defense manufacturing. As we scale, the People team plays a critical role in shaping how we attract, enable, and retain world-class talent across both engineering and advanced manufacturing. Working on the People team at Hadrian means designing and operationalizing the foundation of a company that blends cutting-edge robotics, AI, and precision manufacturing — while supporting a workforce that spans software engineers, machinists, program managers, and everything in between. We’re looking for builders: thoughtful, action-oriented team members who care deeply about people, process, and performance — and who want to help create a company culture that’s as strong as the infrastructure we’re deploying. As a People Program Manager, you’ll drive enterprise-wide initiatives that shape how our People Team operates and delivers impact. In this highly cross-functional role, you'll own the end-to-end delivery of critical people programs - while building the systems, processes, and structures that keep our team aligned, accountable, and moving fast. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role for someone who thrives at the intersection of strategy, operations, and people. If you’re a curious, humble, and analytically-minded individual with a bias toward action and impact, we’d love to hear from you. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Enable People

jobs.description_text: About the Workforce Development Team The Workforce Development team is dedicated to cultivating the next generation of manufacturing talent within a challenging, equitable, and meritocratic environment. Our goal is to accelerate the maturity and operational effectiveness of Hadrian's factories through targeted training programs. The team is responsible for developing and managing a comprehensive training system, driving software adoption, standardizing operational processes, and maintaining an integrated training and certification ecosystem. THE ROLE We are opening a new factory in Muscle Shoals, Alabama, and you will be part of the founding training team. Before our first technicians arrive, you will go through their onboarding and training yourself, test it, and help us refine it so the people who follow have the best possible start. This is a general training role, not tied to a single trade. Deep training experience matters most here. Manufacturing experience is a bonus, and you will learn our production environment through time at our sites in Los Angeles and Arizona and through equipment manufacturer training. WHAT YOU WILL DO Ahead of our first technician cohort, you will experience the technician journey from onboarding through training and qualification, capture what works and what does not, and give clear feedback that shapes the experience before it goes live. jobs.title: Internal Communications & Knowledge Systems Partner
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE: Hadrian is growing fast, and how we share knowledge, make decisions, and communicate is as much a part of what we’re building as anything on the factory floor. We’re looking for an Internal Communications Partner who sees the organization itself as a product, with every employee as a user, and wants to help design how it works. You’re AI forward by default. You’ll think about internal content the way a great product team thinks about product documentation: built around real users, held to a high quality bar, and always current. You’ll shape how information gets created, found, and kept up to date across the company, and set the standards and systems everyone else builds on. This is a chance to define what great looks like from the ground up, at a company where the pace and the stakes are high. You’ll lead the core work of internal comms (announcements, change comms, leadership messaging), and you’ll also build the system underneath it, shaping how Hadrian communicates as it scales. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Own our internal knowledge base as a product. jobs.title: All Levels: Product Engineer
jobs.description_text: The Role Product Engineers at Hadrian are software engineers who own the full product lifecycle, from figuring out what to build to shipping and operating it. You'll work directly with the people running mission-critical manufacturing programs, identify problems worth solving, and turn ambiguous requirements into working software. Much of the work is 0 to 1. You'll build new products, extend existing systems, and help turn successful prototypes into durable platform capabilities. You'll spend most of your time writing code, primarily in React, Next.js, TypeScript, Go, and Python, but we care more about engineering judgment than familiarity with our stack. There's no PM handing you a PRD and no layer between you and your users. Product judgment, technical depth, and the ability to move quickly all matter. The team is early, and the people joining now will have significant influence over both our product direction and how the team operates. No prior aerospace, defense, or manufacturing experience required. What You'll Do - Build and ship full stack products. Take software from an empty repo to production, with real users who depend on it. - Own a product area end to end. jobs.title: Test Engineer
jobs.description_text: The Role Test Engineering is a brand new team at Hadrian, built from the ground up with no legacy test framework to work around. As a Test Engineer, you'll be the responsible engineer and technical lead for all proof and functional testing on a large manufacturing program for complex weldments. You'll set the test strategy for the program and decide what we test, how, and why. You'll use engineering first principles to decide which requirements we meet, exceed, or push back on, and you'll make the calls on cost, schedule, quality, and safety. You'll lead the design of the test equipment, make sure every test is safe, and coordinate the engineers and technicians who build and run it. You'll be on the floor for first articles, hand each test off to production, and set the standards the team carries to the next program. The program is in its development phase today, and scope will grow as it moves into production. Many of the test capabilities will take 6 to 12 months to build, so the work you do now shapes how the factory runs later. If you like building a test program from an empty floor, leading through your expertise, and owning the outcome, this role is for you. jobs.title: Corporate Finance Associate
jobs.description_text: THE ROLE: The Operational Finance team at Hadrian drives both the strategic direction and the day-to-day execution of our advanced manufacturing mission. We partner closely with Manufacturing Operations, Engineering, and Business leadership to build the company plan and the models, processes, and financial frameworks behind our biggest decisions. As a Senior Corporate Finance Associate, you’ll own the central company forecast, which is the single view of where Hadrian is heading. You will be in charge of consolidating changes from the Finance team, Operations, and functional leaders and reporting high-level financials to the senior leadership. You will provide the foundation upon which decisions related to M&A, growth opportunities, fundraising, and company planning are made. You will be responsible for coordinating with the rest of the finance team, individual program owners and experts and ensure we have a highly accurate and detailed view of the company. You will continuously improve the overall forecasting process and help develop systems that are used to update and maintain the forecast and its outputs. You’ll also work with central FP&A to incorporate program forecasts into the company plan and bring execution reality into the deal-making process so that future contracts and financing are structured appropriately. You’ll own strategy and execution for indirect and non-production spend, including services, software, facilities, IT, and R&D purchases, and you’ll lead buyers who manage those categories day to day. jobs.title: Sr. Cost Control Engineer
jobs.description_text: The role We are hiring a Cost Control Engineer to own the cost baseline, the forecast, and change control on Mariana's capital projects. You will build the cost breakdown structure, convert the sanctioned estimate into a control budget, track commitments and actuals, and produce the forecast at completion that the business plans against. The role sits between engineering, procurement, construction, and finance — the path where a commitment becomes an accrual becomes an invoice becomes a capitalized asset — and your job is to make sure the number is the same in all four places. Cost control here is not a monthly report assembled by hand. The reporting is expected to come out of the system and building that pipeline is as much the job as running it. What you'll do - Set the baseline. Build the WBS and cost breakdown structure with the planner and estimator, convert the sanctioned estimate into a control budget, and lock it - Track commitments and actuals. Purchase orders, subcontracts, change orders, and field costs, reconciled to the ERP every month with no unexplained variance - Forecast. Maintain estimate to complete and estimate at completion by control account, with the basis for each forecast written down rather than carried in your head - Measure earned value. Set rules of credit with the planner, measure physical progress, and report cost and schedule performance at a level where someone can act on it - Run the trend and change process. jobs.title: AI Automation Engineer, Real-World Test Lab
jobs.description_text: About the Real-World Test Lab Physical AI doesn't get graded on a leaderboard. It gets graded on a factory floor at shift change, in a substation with no GPS, on a site where the lighting is wrong and the stakes are real. The Real-World Test Lab closes the gap between the benchmark and the field. We bring the customer's world inside our walls - their devices, their environments, their hardest conditions, and their definition of success - and make it the bar every release has to clear. As Niantic Spatial's first and most demanding customer, we push our reconstruction, localization, and spatial understanding to their limits, find where they shine and where they break, and turn that into evidence that shapes what we build next. It's a new team at the frontier of physical AI, and you'll help invent how the job is done. About the Role We're hiring an AI Automation Engineer, reporting to the Director of the Real-World Test Lab, to build the system that produces our evidence. Today our evaluations are manual, inconsistent, and slow. You'll design and own the automation that runs them end to end on every relevant release, with no human driving it, turning one-off experiments into an always-on service the whole company relies on. This role is about owning the evidence, not executing a test plan. jobs.title: Senior Computer Vision Engineer, Embodied AI
jobs.description_text: We're looking for a Senior Computer Vision Engineer to join our Embodied AI team, focused on 3D scene understanding and semantics. A reconstructed environment is only useful to a robot once it knows what is in it: which surfaces are floor, which objects can be grasped, moved, or opened, where one room ends and another begins. You'll work hand in hand with our Research Scientists to take advances in open-vocabulary perception, 3D semantic labeling, and scene graph construction and turn them into reliable capabilities that embodied AI teams can use in production. This is an applied research role. You'll live at the boundary between a research prototype and a production pipeline: adapting methods so they hold up on messy customer captures, lifting 2D semantic signals into geometrically consistent 3D, defining what "semantically correct" means for a downstream policy, and feeding what you learn back into the research agenda. You understand that the difficult part is often not the core method, but the messy inputs, edge cases, operational constraints, and downstream requirements surrounding it. You care about quality, cost, latency, and reliability, and you know that a system is only successful when people can depend on it. This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who wants to build, ship, and own outcomes. jobs.title: AI Engineer, Computer Vision
jobs.description_text: About the Team Localization is where the map meets the moment. Our localization team builds the living geospatial world model and the centimeter-level Visual Positioning System (VPS) that lets people and robots know exactly where they are, from any camera, almost anywhere on Earth. That system is learned, not hand-built. Our localization stack has moved from classical geometry to visual models trained on billions of posed images — models that have to be accurate to the centimeter, robust to lighting and seasons and clutter, and fast enough to run in production for every query. This team sits at the junction of research and production: we take what works in a paper, make it work on our data, and make it work for customers. About the Role We're hiring an AI Engineer, Computer Vision, to contribute to the deep learning models at the heart of our localization system. Working alongside experienced researchers and engineers, you'll help train and iterate on the visual models — feature extractors, matchers, pose regressors, and retrieval models — that turn a single image into a precise position in the world. This is a full-loop environment. You'll get exposure to the entire pipeline: the data the model learns on, training, evaluation, and the service that runs it in production. You'll be surrounded by people who care deeply about correctness — where a loss curve going down is not the same as a system getting better — and you'll grow into that rigor quickly. jobs.description_text: Role Northwood engineers and operators run hardware and software across a global network of antenna ground stations and the cloud services behind them. No one sells a platform for running a network like this at scale, so Northwood builds its own. Platform Engineering builds the software that takes Northwood products from first prototype to full operation. That covers how code is built, tested, and released, how every site and service is monitored, and how hardware in remote locations is brought online, updated, and kept healthy. Every one of these problems has to work across every site, service, and customer at once. Few organizations get to build this kind of software in house. What this team builds will shape how a global network of antennas is operated for the missions that depend on it. Every new antenna, site, and customer Northwood adds runs on this platform, and it sets how fast the network can grow. As an early-career Software Engineer on the Platform team, you'll ship to real production systems from your first weeks, with close mentorship, and take on more ownership as you show you're ready. You don't need to know every part of the stack today. You need to learn fast, reason clearly through problems you haven't seen before, and care a lot about what you build. jobs.title: Head of AI
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Osmo is building the first computer that can smell. Olfactory Intelligence (OI) is the model suite behind that: it predicts how a molecule or a mixture will smell, generates new formulas from a creative brief, and now powers commercial products for some of the largest consumer goods companies in the world. It runs on 5.4M+ human sniff annotations, 100M+ mass spectral readings, and a molecule library in the billions, data no one else has. We are hiring a Head of Applied AI to own the team that builds these models. You will lead the ML engineers and research scientists, set the roadmap and the quality bar, and own the path from research notebook to production API. jobs.title: Contract Sensory Evaluator Panelist (Fragrance)
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE Osmo is seeking a highly meticulous and olfactively acute individual to join our team as Contract Sensory Panelist (Fragrance). This is a specialized, part-time contract role dedicated exclusively to generating high-quality sensory data that fuels our Olfactory Intelligence models. It's work that rewards genuine curiosity about scent and the tenacity to stay sharp through long, repetitive evaluation sessions. We collaborate closely with hardware engineers, camera tuning experts, and flight test engineers to optimize the performance of drone imaging systems. We employ data-driven testing approaches, using massive amounts of flight data to assess image quality and overall system stability. Our tools include Imatest for data analysis, custom-built logging systems, and proprietary tools for testing image quality in various lighting conditions. About the role: Skydio is seeking an enthusiastic Flight Test Engineer with a strong understanding of cameras and image quality to ensure that the units we are shipping to customers are of the highest standard. This role requires a rigorous approach to testing complex systems, particularly the camera components, across a wide spectrum of environmental and operating conditions, ensuring the overall system performs optimally. As a Flight Test Engineer focused on Camera and Image Quality, you will be critical in ensuring that Skydio’s drones deliver unparalleled imaging performance across a wide range of environmental conditions. Your expertise in camera systems will be essential as you run field tests, identify and troubleshoot issues, and collaborate with various teams to optimize product performance. jobs.title: Software Engineer Intern - Summer 2027
jobs.description_text: About the role: With best-in-class autonomy and real-time cloud connectivity, drones are becoming critical infrastructure for solving real-world problems faster, safer, and more efficiently. Our customers, from public safety agencies to industrial and enterprise operators, rely on Skydio Cloud to plan missions, manage fleets, and make sense of the data their drones collect. As a Software Engineering Intern, you’ll help build the systems and features that power autonomous drone operations at scale. You’ll work across the stack, from backend services in Python and Go to frontend experiences in TypeScript and React, and you’ll own meaningful pieces of work from idea to shipped feature. Our team works on a wide range of challenges and we go where we’re needed: - Building customer-facing features in the Skydio Cloud web app, such as fleet health monitoring, media asset management, and device management - Designing and extending the APIs and data models that connect drones, docks, and the data they produce - Visualizing rich spatial data through maps and 3D views - Improving the reliability, performance, and observability of the systems behind it all The variety of work means there are plenty of opportunities to learn and have a meaningful impact on how Skydio builds and delivers software. jobs.title: Director, NPI Operations Engineering
jobs.description_text: About the Role: The NPI Operations Engineering leader builds and leads the team responsible for making Skydio's next generation of autonomous robotics, including drones, docks and accessories, at our internal manufacturing facility in Hayward. You’ll deliver the process, manufacturing know-how and technology needed to build the most capable flying robots on the planet. The team combines Manufacturing Design Engineering and Supply Base Engineering into one organization that is 100% focused on new product development. You will own the manufacturability of every new product: assembly time, assembly yield and the processes, fixtures, equipment and supplier readiness needed to hit them. You and your team will engage with Product Engineering from early architecture, carry products through EVT, DVT and PVT, and hand them to Process Engineering for sustaining once they meet clear production-readiness criteria. This is a leadership role with significant scope to shape how Skydio develops hardware. You'll set the team's direction, hire and grow engineers, and be the single operations voice in product development. Sustaining engineering for products already in production sits with Process Engineering, so this team stays focused on getting new products right before they reach the line. jobs.title: Senior Hardware Product Packaging Engineer
jobs.description_text: About the role: Packaging is the first thing a customer sees and touches and the last mile between our hardware and our customers. A Skydio drone might ship across the country in a corrugated carton, live for three years in a hard case in the trunk of a patrol car, get thrown in the back of a utility truck, or be carried into the field on a soldier’s back — and it has to work every time it comes out. You will own the designs that make that workflow possible: the unboxing moment, the field case, the foam, the labeling, and the pack-out on our production line. This is a highly cross-functional role sitting between design, manufacturing, supply chain, and our vendors. How you’ll make an impact: - Own customer-facing and enterprise-ready packaging from concept to mass production across Skydio’s full product ecosystem including aircraft, docks, controllers, batteries, attachments, and accessories. jobs.title: Senior Flight Test Engineer - Software Automation
jobs.description_text: About the role: Autonomous drones are complex systems operating in uncontrolled environments. Onboard autonomy and hardware have to work together on every flight, along with the mobile and browser interfaces that control them. Testing these systems is one of the most critical parts of delivering a reliable product. We are looking for an experienced Software Automation Engineer to lead the Flight Test Automation Pod and scale how we validate autonomous flight. You will design and own automated test systems that run from CI through simulation, hardware-in-the-loop and real-world flight. You’ll bring AI-supported workflows into how tests are written, run and analyzed, and define how we measure test coverage, so every release ships with confidence. This position is part of the Product Integrity organization, which owns product quality from NPI through end of life across hardware and software. Your work will directly shape how quickly and reliably Skydio ships new capabilities to customers. How you'll make an impact: - Lead the Flight Test Automation Pod: set technical direction, own the roadmap, and mentor engineers who contribute to automation - Own automated test workflows across mobile, browser, and integrated hardware/software systems, from simulation to real-world flight - Establish and own CI test pipelines that validate every build automatically and give developers fast, actionable feedback - Design an extensible test framework that scales across teams, making it easy for

jobs.description_text: THE CHALLENGE Our products are used by professionals with a lot on the line, operating in rugged environments where every second counts. Their mission is clear: find the missing person, get the lights back on, keep the roads open, and keep the good guys safe. To win, our products must be more than just capable, they must be undeniably reliable. We are looking for a UX Product Designer who understands that trust isn't a buzzword; it's built through absolute system transparency, pragmatic workflows, and giving the operator a clear handle to grab when things get chaotic. Our UX Product Designers are inventing the interfaces of the future. You will not be designing generic dashboards. You will be helping to design the critical trust-bridge between human operators and advanced AI hardware, translating extreme technological complexity into intuitive, reliable, and beautiful experiences. jobs.title: Frontend Software Engineer Intern - Summer 2027
jobs.description_text: About the role Skydio’s mission is to make the world safer and more efficient through autonomous drones.
